newsitem.title: SPAIN: TENNIS-GERMAN PAIR REVIVE DAVIS CUP HOPES WITH DOUBLES WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GERMAN PAIR REVIVE DAVIS CUP HOPES WITH DOUBLES WIN.

text.p: Germany's Marc Goellner kept his country's Davis Cup hopes alive by partnering David Prinosil to a comprehensive doubles victory over Spaniards Alex Corretja and Carlos Costa on Saturday.

The Olympic bronze medallists completely outclassed Corretja and Costa 6-2 6-2 6-3 in their world group first round tie, but Spain take a 2-1 lead into Sunday's decisive singles matches and remain firm favourites to win the tie.
"(On Friday) they said we couldn't play any worse," said Goellner, who lost his singles rubber in straight sets to Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya. "Now we've got a chance, we're alive again."
Both Spaniards were broken as games went against serve at the beginning of the first set, but the German pair were quicker to settle and returned serve superbly.
"They were much better than us," said Spanish coach Manolo Santana, who has struggled for years to find a winning doubles combination.
"I have to find the (right) pair, I'm sure I will find it some day."
On Sunday, Hendrik Dreekman, who went down in straight sets on Friday to world number 11 Albert Costa, will meet Moya.
"If Dreekman wins, so will I," said Goellner, who will play the last rubber against Costa.
